messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary rollout starting for model 'riff-v2' (canary group: 5%) to prod then failing health checks. Error rate spike from 0.3% -> 22% over last 3 min. Observed errors: TokenizerMismatch and model inference exceptions. Paging on-call (olivia). Link: https://redwood.internal/deploys/3782

pagerduty: Paging alert triggered for oncall olivia (incident: INC-2026-0423). Priority: P1. See alerts: https://pagerduty.local/INC-2026-0423

olivia: I'm on it — grabbing context. Which deploy changed tokenizer? @sanjay any recent model build?

sanjay: I pushed riff-v2 yesterday, changed quantization + moved to new tokenizer v3 (different vocab). Verified locally. CI model tests passed. No change to serving config AFAIK.

ken: seeing heap of errors in canary logs: `TokenizerMismatch: expected vocab_size 50257 got 30000` from model runner at startup for several shards. Full snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T10:23:41Z] ERROR model-runner - TokenizerMismatch: expected vocab_size 50257 got 30000
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/runtime/serve.py", line 421, in load_model
    tokenizer = Tokenizer.load(cfg.tokenizer_path)
  File "/opt/runtime/tokenizer.py", line 88, in load
    raise TokenizerMismatch(err)
```

emily: quick check: did the config reference a different tokenizer path in the deployment manifest? I see `tokenizer_path: /models/tokenizers/riff-v1` in prod config and built artifact uses `/models/tokenizers/riff-v2` in package. That smells like config drift during deploy.

sanjay: ugh — the build pipeline updated artifact but the deploy job grabbed the older config blob from `deploy-configs/prod` bucket. Probably a timing issue; version pin mismatch.

olivia: assessment: canary is failing due to tokenizer mismatch. Customer impact: several transient 503s for text-gen endpoints routed to canary. CS reports two customers with degraded UX. Escalating to P1.

cs-team: We've received 3 customer tickets (IDs: #4201, #4204, #4207) complaining about 502/503 on text-gen since 10:22. No data exfiltration. Priority: high.

ken: mitigation plan: (1) kill canary traffic via feature-flag / kill-switch; (2) rollback canary to riff-v1.9 or pin tokenizer path; (3) investigate pipeline race. I'll perform steps 1 and 2 unless objections.

olivia: go for it. Please announce each action in thread.

ken: running kill-switch now: `/ff toggle canary_riff_v2 false --env=prod`

deploy-bot: Feature flag `canary_riff_v2` toggled to `false` by ken at 2026-03-15T10:26:12Z. Traffic to riff-v2 canary lanes should drain in ~30s.

ken: initiating rollback: `deploy rollback --deployment riff-v2-canary --to-tag riff-v1.9 --wait`

deploy-bot: Rollback started for riff-v2-canary -> riff-v1.9. Steps: drain -> deploy riff-v1.9 -> warm KV caches. ETA ~2m.

olivia: CS notified customers that we are rolling back and working on fix. Patch note to customers sent at 10:27.

sanjay: quick fix would also be to update the prod config blob to point tokenizer_path -> `/models/tokenizers/riff-v2` and restart canary, but prefer rollback until we confirm pipeline fix.

ken: rollback completed: `deploy status` shows riff-v1.9 active for canary lanes. Health checks green. Verified by hitting canary endpoint 10x: all responses 200 and tokenization correct. :white_check_mark:

emily: monitoring: error rate dropped back to baseline within ~90s after rollback. No further 5xx spikes on main route.

olivia: handing off to sanjay for root cause and remediation. I'll stay on until we have a short writeup. Sanjay, please take ownership for pipeline fix + postmortem.

sanjay: taking lead. Immediate next steps: (1) git revert in `deploy-configs` to ensure artifact/config pin remains atomic; (2) add CI guard comparing artifact tokenizer_path vs deploy config; (3) postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-15 15:00 (invite sent).

cs-team: customers updated: tickets moved to monitoring, CS will follow up with customers in 1h and offer credits if needed. No data loss.

olivia: incident declared resolved for live traffic. Severity: P1 -> reduced to P2 pending postmortem. Thanks all. Closing timeline entry and creating incident postmortem doc. :tada:
